mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates fewer commuting trips, which suppresses impulse shopping and after-work visits to retail areas. If this commuting contraction persists, RETAIL_REC should stay below its prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above the previous 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remaining below baseline for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays near or above baseline while WORKPLACES falls, more activity shifts to home-centered routines and discretionary shopping is deferred. This home-stay substitution should push RETAIL_REC downward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 points while RESIDENTIAL is at or above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after WORKPLACES crosses below -20 while RESIDENTIAL remains nonnegative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS reflects reduced leisure outings and generally weaker off-work mobility, which spills over into fewer combined shopping trips. If PARKS continues to fall, RETAIL_REC should decline further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stabilizes while PARKS remains materially below baseline for the full next four-week window.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both keep sliding, the city is likely in a mobility-tightening phase that reduces access to shopping districts and short-notice retail visits. Under that tightening regime, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each decline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep declining for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A deterioration in GROCERY_PHARM signals more essential-trip suppression and weaker neighborhood circulation, which typically spills into fewer add-on retail visits. Once grocery mobility turns negative, RETAIL_REC should fall within the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop in the week after GROCERY_PHARM first moves below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If the gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows because grocery trips are falling faster than retail visits, it implies households are consolidating errands without expanding discretionary shopping. That consolidation should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines more than 3 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC remains below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean during a period when GROCERY_PHARM is falling faster than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained negative summer leisure shock is visible when PARKS and TRANSIT both weaken together, indicating fewer discretionary outings and weaker access to destination retail. In that seasonal pattern, RETAIL_REC should continue to trend down over two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days even though both PARKS and TRANSIT stay below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in TRANSIT from its current low level would restore access to shopping corridors faster than workplace mobility recovers, producing a lagged rebound in retail foot traffic. If transit stops falling and turns up, RETAIL_REC should improve within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks after being below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 28-day mean after TRANSIT has risen for two straight weeks from below -15.
